tasks.short: Answer client questions and advise on future tax choices.

steps.what: Read the client's question and identify the advice needed.
Gather the tax return, financial records and relevant client history.
Research applicable rules and note their relevance to the client's circumstances.

loop.input: Advice scope, client evidence pack and retrieved tax sources filtered by jurisdiction and tax year.
loop.output: Applicability notes with citations, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source dates and citation passages automatically; the tax preparer verifies legal applicability.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; conflicting or missing authority returns to manual research.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search can retrieve sources, but relating their prose to unusual client facts needs interpretation.

steps.what: Calculate alternative outcomes using the tax preparation system or a spreadsheet.
Discuss scenarios, clarify priorities and recommend a suitable course.
Write an advice note recording assumptions, recommendations and next actions.

loop.input: Structured agreed advice, verified applicability notes and calculated tax scenarios.
loop.output: Draft advice note with assumptions, citations and next actions.
loop.check: Every amount must match a scenario; every recommendation must match the recorded agreed advice.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; failed checks leave a template for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but explanations vary with the client's priorities and circumstances.

steps.what: Check and send the advice note to the client.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles records from the tax preparation system in {OTHER}, the {ERP}, the {CRM} and {DOCS}, then runs versioned scenario calculations. A bounded drafting loop prepares cited research notes and an advice note; the tax preparer verifies the interpretation, holds the client conversation and approves sending through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were scattered, tax sources changed, and client-specific explanations took time to write.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and calculation engines can be stitched together faster with AI-assisted coding. Bounded drafting can work from verified facts and approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-border situations, incomplete facts and uncertain future law remain expensive. GDPR applies to client data; EU AI Act duties depend on the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the client values, challenge risky assumptions and explain trade-offs the client can act on.

ambition.what: Pre-year-end tax scenario consultation for small-business clients.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling files to discussing choices and resolving uncertain cases. The preparer can propose scenario consultations; authority to approve tax positions does not automatically expand.

reach.task: Compare cash-flow outcomes across tax scenarios.
reach.learn: Cash-flow modelling, sensitivity analysis and the limits of the preparer's advice remit.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas supports income and corporate tax returns while the user remains responsible; this supports assisted preparation, not autonomous advice.
Versioned arithmetic can calculate scenarios; suitability and client priorities require human judgement.
GPT for Work reports incorrect cash-waterfall results in its model benchmark, supporting independent checks of generated figures.

assumptions: The setting is a tax practice within a mid-size European professional-services company.
{OTHER} denotes the tax preparation system throughout this job.
Advice involves substantial conversation, so the communication prior outweighs the low meeting share.
Remaining time estimates are design hypotheses; new exception work is additional.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, tax years and client types the practice serves.
Whether the tax preparation system provides scenario calculations and usable exports.
Which sources the practice licenses and approves.
Whether employee consultation is required under national rules for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which recurring questions can use approved scenario templates?
How accurately can research drafts distinguish enacted rules from proposals?
Which scenario checks catch errors before advice reaches a client?
new_work: Verify cited interpretations and approve outgoing advice notes.
Resolve missing records and conflicting client facts.
Maintain tax-year rules, calculation tests and source permissions.
Monitor drafting failures and integration access.

tasks.short: Research tax procedures for unusual returns.

steps.what: Define the unusual issue, jurisdiction, tax year and missing facts.
Search handbooks, official bulletins and previously documented treatments.
Read relevant passages and compare conditions, exclusions and effective dates.

loop.input: Retrieved passages, source metadata, research question and relevant client facts.
loop.output: Comparison of conditions, exclusions, dates and unresolved conflicts with exact citations.
loop.check: Verify quotations against source text and dates against metadata; the preparer reads decisive passages.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; absent or conflicting sources trigger manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search cannot reliably compare qualifications expressed differently across legal prose.

steps.what: Choose the preparation procedure and resolve remaining legal uncertainty.
Record the chosen procedure, supporting citations and outstanding conditions.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable source library in {DOCS} with jurisdiction, effective dates and links to the {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded loop prepares a cited comparison, while the tax preparer chooses the treatment; a template then records that approved choice in {DOCS} and the tax preparation system in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source collections had uneven metadata, and legal qualifications required careful reading. Reusable research notes were difficult to find.
tasks.enabler_now: Search configuration, source indexing and template generation are established tools. A bounded model can compare retrieved passages while preserving their provenance.
tasks.still_hard: Access to licensed sources, historical versions and conflicting interpretations remains costly. GDPR requires controlled use of client facts; national rules govern professional responsibilities.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a superficially similar precedent does not apply and decide when specialist advice is needed.

ambition.what: Internal atypical-return consultation desk for bookkeeping staff.

tasks.altitude: The preparer spends less time searching and more time testing interpretations. They can provide documented consultations to bookkeeping staff, while existing escalation limits still apply.

reach.task: Assess how an unusual tax treatment affects accounting entries and disclosures.
reach.learn: Book-to-tax differences, supporting workpapers and disclosure materiality.

evidence.claim: Search, source metadata and templates can reduce research administration without deciding legal applicability.
AFAS Jonas provides assistance within tax returns while leaving responsibility with the user; it does not establish reliable atypical-return legal research.

assumptions: Most source reading is digital, consistent with the document-heavy prior.
Search assistance offers gains even though selecting an atypical treatment remains human.
Existing search configuration is sufficient once sources have usable metadata.
The tax preparer may approve treatments within existing competence limits.
unknowns: Source licensing terms and availability of historical versions.
The practice's specialist escalation and second-review thresholds.
Whether existing research notes contain reusable, verified citations.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the planned tools.
research_questions: Can retrieval find all decisive exclusions in a sample of past atypical returns?
Which sources need manual indexing or access?
What makes a treatment note reusable without exposing client information?
new_work: Maintain source dates, versions and licensing permissions.
Review comparisons and escalate uncertain interpretations.
Retire treatment notes when law or official guidance changes.
Check retrieval failures against completed research cases.

tasks.short: Calculate preparation fees from return complexity and required processing time.

steps.what: Review return features and processing-time records in the tax preparation system.
Consult the applicable fee schedule and engagement terms.
Calculate the base fee, complexity supplements and time charges.
Assess discounts, unusual effort and departures from agreed pricing.
Record the approved fee and calculation basis for billing.

tasks.design: A small fee calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines return features from the tax preparation system in {OTHER}, time records from {PROJECT} and versioned fee rules held in {WORKFLOW}. It produces an explainable calculation, routes pricing departures to the authorised person and writes the approved fee to the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complexity categories and engagement exceptions were not consistently encoded. Manual transfers connected return records, time records and billing.
tasks.enabler_now: Rules, forms and integrations can be built quickly with AI-assisted coding. The calculation itself needs ordinary arithmetic and versioned pricing rules.
tasks.still_hard: Estimating effort before work begins and handling ambiguous engagement terms remain judgement calls. Poor time records weaken profitability analysis.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish legitimate extra scope from avoidable rework and negotiate a fair fee.

ambition.what: Weekly review of preparation margin by return type.

tasks.altitude: The preparer handles scope and pricing exceptions instead of rebuilding fee calculations. With explicit delegation, they can adjust fees within approved bands; broader pricing changes remain with the practice manager.

reach.task: Review service margins and recommend changes to preparation fees.
reach.learn: Cost allocation, realised hourly rates and pricing sensitivity.

reach.task: Turn approved fee records into accurate invoices.
reach.learn: Billing codes, adjustment handling and duplicate prevention.

evidence.claim: Fee arithmetic and rule selection can use deterministic code when complexity categories and engagement terms are structured.
Negotiated discounts and uncertain scope require judgement; the digest provides no direct fee-calculation case.

assumptions: A spreadsheet often connects fee rules to tax and time records in this setting.
Routine calculations have higher rule coverage than the judgement-heavy prior suggests.
The preparer approves fees within existing limits and escalates larger departures.
Engagement exceptions are encoded by a person rather than interpreted by a model.
unknowns: Whether existing systems already support the required fee rules.
Which fees use fixed prices, actual time or estimated time.
How reliably staff record processing time and return complexity.
Who may approve discounts and pricing departures.
Whether time-data reuse needs consultation under national rules.
research_questions: How many historical fees can the current schedule reproduce exactly?
Which complexity features predict effort without subjective scoring?
Can existing configuration remove the need for a custom calculator?
new_work: Maintain fee schedules, effective dates and exception thresholds.
Correct missing complexity fields and unreliable time records.
Review pricing departures and monitor fee-to-invoice reconciliation.
Maintain integrations and calculation regression checks.

tasks.short: Arrange client appointments and send confirmations.

steps.what: Read the appointment request and identify duration, purpose and access needs.
Check staff availability, meeting duration and filing deadlines.
Exchange proposed times with the client until a slot is agreed.
Create the calendar appointment and send the client a confirmation.
Send a reminder with the appointment details and document checklist.

tasks.design: Configure client booking against the {CALENDAR}, using structured appointment types, availability rules and deadline buffers. The client selects a slot; the {WORKFLOW} creates the appointment and sends confirmations and reminders through {EMAIL}, while unusual requests enter a staff queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability and appointment requirements were handled through individual mailboxes. Booking rules had not been agreed or configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar booking, structured forms and scheduled reminders are established capabilities. Routine scheduling needs configuration rather than a model.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent cases, accessibility needs, cancellations and multi-person meetings still require coordination. Calendar details must follow GDPR data minimisation; national rules may affect staff-calendar access.
tasks.human_edge: Accommodate distressed clients and decide which urgent appointment deserves scarce capacity.

ambition.what: Self-service booking for shift workers who cannot call during office hours.

tasks.altitude: Routine scheduling leaves the preparer's week; exceptions and client care remain. They may prioritise urgent appointments within agreed capacity limits, without gaining authority over colleagues' working hours.

reach.task: Forecast appointment capacity around filing deadlines.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, appointment demand and deadline bottlenecks.

evidence.claim: Existing calendar and workflow capabilities can provide booking, confirmations and reminders without model reasoning.
Routine client-selected bookings can operate within approved availability rules without staff approval of each appointment.

assumptions: The baseline describes manually arranged appointments; some practices already automate them.
Mailbox exchanges take more time than the weak mail-share prior suggests.
Clients provide structured booking requirements and select their own slot.
Routine booking authority is delegated through approved calendar rules.
Zero remaining time applies to routine steps; exception handling remains additional work.
unknowns: Whether the existing {CALENDAR} supports external booking and required appointment types.
How often appointments need several staff members or special accommodation.
Which calendar access and consultation arrangements national rules require.
Whether clients need a telephone alternative.
Who may override deadline buffers and reserved capacity.
research_questions: Which appointment types can be booked without staff intervention?
How should urgent cases reach a person without exposing tax details?
Which reminder timing reduces missed appointments for these clients?
new_work: Handle urgent requests, special accommodations and booking failures.
Maintain appointment durations, buffers and staff availability.
Update document checklists and reminder templates.
Review access permissions and calendar synchronisation failures.

role.altitude: The tax preparer spends more of the week on client choices, atypical treatments and scope exceptions. Proposed delegation covers routine booking and bounded fee adjustments; substantive tax advice remains professionally accountable.
reach: Support accountants and auditors with documented book-to-tax treatment analysis.
Help financial managers review preparation margins and seasonal capacity.
Give billing clerks traceable approved fee records.
skills_to_grow: Scenario modelling and explanation of uncertainty.
Client interviewing and practical tax planning.
Data access, exception handling and integration checks.
role.ambitious_version: Combine pre-year-end scenario consultations with an internal atypical-return desk, supported by traceable calculations and reviewed research. Use preparation margins and appointment demand to propose better service packages and seasonal staffing.
